lines.trans: Well, how do you like the dish?
For a starter it will do.
So bring out the ribs already.
Haute cuisine is not a snack for you.
And thirdly, what, Vitya?
Not Vitya, but Viktor Petrovich.
You should not act like that, Viktor Petrovich.
After all, the earth is round.
And who is going to pay?
Why, I did not even eat anything.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('platter') (large flat serving dish) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'thirdly / third of all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Third of all, I am in a great mood.

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно в-третьих и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite thirdly and calmly.

meanings.note: Adds a reason or an obvious truth. Core Russian part meaning 'after all, you know' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I did tell you, you know!

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come back, to return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'сокий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('high, tall').
на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: В дорогу = for the journey. Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'рога'). Common feminine noun meaning 'road; way' in everyday Russian.
В дорогу = for the journey. Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'рога'). Common feminine noun meaning 'road; way' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: not to be confused with есть 'there is' (from быть)

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'appetizer'.
Genitive: земли. Common feminine noun meaning 'ground, earth, land' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A meter fifty off the ground!

examples.text: Вот так, Даня! Метр пятьдесят от земли!

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чало'). Common neuter noun meaning 'beginning' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: At the beginning of the week.

examples.text: Ваня, это теперь твоё. И это только начало.
examples.trans: Vanya, this is yours now. And it's only the beginning.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
